## Window Header and Title Bar
- **Application Name**: Visual Studio Code
- **Date and Time**: Oct 22 23:36
- **System Tray Icons**: Located at the top-right corner, including system status icons (network, sound, power)
- **Window Controls**: Minimize, Maximize, Close buttons at the top-right corner
- **Application Icon**: VS Code logo at the top-left corner

## Menu Bar
- **Menu Items**: File, Edit, Selection, View, Go, Run, Terminal, Help
- **Active Menu**: File is highlighted, indicating it is currently selected or hovered

## Left Sidebar (Activity Bar)
- **Icons and Functions**:
  - **Explorer**: Currently active, indicated by a blue icon and text
  - **Search**: Magnifying glass icon
  - **Source Control**: Branch icon
  - **Debug**: Bug icon
  - **Extensions**: Square grid icon
  - **Remote Explorer**: Server icon
  - **Git**: Git icon
  - **Terminal**: Terminal icon
  - **Settings**: Gear icon
  - **Outline**: Document icon
  - **Timeline**: Timeline icon
  - **User Profile**: Person icon
  - **Grid Icon**: App launcher icon
- **Status Indicators**:
  - **Notifications**: A notification badge with the number 1 on the Settings gear icon
  - **Status Bar**: At the bottom of the sidebar, showing icons for Git status (0 commits, 0 changes, 0 conflicts)

## Explorer Panel
- **Status**: NO FOLDER OPENED
- **Message**: You have not yet opened a folder.
- **Actions**:
  - **Open Folder**: Blue button
  - **Clone Repository**: Blue button
- **Additional Information**:
  - Opening a folder will close all currently open editors.
  - To keep them open, add a folder instead.
  - You can clone a repository locally.
  - Link to documentation: "To learn more about how to use Git and source control in VS Code read our docs."

## Main Content Area
- **Active Tab**: Settings
- **Search Bar**:
  - **Search Query**: "workspace trust enabled"
  - **Results Count**: 7 Settings Found
  - **Filter Icon**: Filter icon next to the results count
- **Settings Categories**:
  - **User** (selected)
  - **Workbench (1)**
  - **Window (1)**
  - **Features (1)**
  - **Extensions (1)**
  - **Security (4)**
  - **Workspace (4)**
- **Settings Details**:
  - **Security > Workspace > Trust: Enabled** (Applies to all profiles)
    - Description: Controls whether or not Workspace Trust is enabled within VS Code.
    - Checkbox: Unchecked
  - **Workbench > Trusted Domains: Prompt In Trusted Workspace** (Applies to all profiles)
    - Description: When enabled, trusted domain prompts will appear when opening links in trusted workspaces.
    - Checkbox: Unchecked
  - **Extensions: Support Untrusted Workspaces** (Applies to all profiles)
    - Description: Override the untrusted workspace support of an extension. Extensions using true will always be enabled. Extensions using limited will always be enabled, and the extension will hide functionality that requires trust. Extensions using false will only be enabled only when the workspace is trusted.
    - Link: Edit in settings.json
  - **Window: Title** (Applies to all profiles)
    - Description: Controls the window title based on the current context such as the opened workspace or active editor. Variables are substituted based on the context.
    - List of Variables:
      - ${activeEditorShort}: the file name (e.g. myFile.txt)
      - ${activeEditorMedium}: the path of the file relative to the workspace folder (e.g. myFolder/myFileFolder/myFile.txt)
      - ${activeEditorLong}: the full path of the file (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder/myFileFolder/myFile.txt)
      - ${activeFolderShort}: the name of the folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFileFolder)
      - ${activeFolderMedium}: the path of the folder the file is contained in, relative to the workspace folder (e.g. myFolder/myFileFolder)
      - ${activeFolderLong}: the full path of the folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder/myFileFolder)
      - ${folderName}: name of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFolder)
      - ${folderPath}: file path of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder)
      - ${rootName}: name of the workspace with optional remote name and workspace indicator if applicable
